claims.text: MEASURED 2026-07-30: `specificity`, `commit_shas` and `measure_commit` are defined BELOW the `if __name__` block and this function is defined above them, so no committed command could reach the specificity arm at all.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the `if __name__` block or definitions of specificity, commit_shas, measure_commit. The claim refers to code outside this chunk.

claims.text: The published false-alarm figures (0.9% refs, 0.7% structure) were produced by a throwaway script during a session and could not be regenerated by anyone afterwards -- a measurement without a command is a measurement without provenance, which this repository treats as no measurement.
claims.why: The claim refers to external published figures and a throwaway script; no code in this chunk can verify or refute it.

claims.text: Detection rate over a MECHANICALLY generated corpus, per operator.
claims.why: The function held_out generates a corpus mechanically via mutate.generate and returns per-operator detection rates.

claims.text: MEASURED 2026-07-30, and the reason this exists as a function rather than as a number in a document: the published 75.3% held-out figure had **no committed command**. It was produced by a throwaway script inside a session and nobody -- including its author -- could regenerate it afterwards. This repository treats a measurement without a command as a measurement without provenance, which is to say as no measurement at all.
claims.why: The claim references a published 75.3% figure and a throwaway script; no code in this chunk can verify that figure or the history. The function itself is present, but the claim about the past is not checkable.

claims.text: Held out in the meaningful sense: :mod:`daedalus.eval.mutate` builds the corpus from the tree by rule, with no knowledge of what the scoring layers look at, so nothing here was tuned against these specific mutants.
claims.why: The claim depends on the behavior of mutate.generate (outside this chunk) and the scoring layers (also outside). The chunk contains no evidence that the scoring layers are independent.

claims.text: Scored on the CLEAN arm only. The three layers are applied to a function's source before and after mutation, and a mutant counts as detected if any of them moves.
claims.why: The code in held_out applies three layers (refs, literals, structure) to before and after, and counts detected if moved. The returned dict includes arm: 'clean (code.refs.ast + literals + structure); no leaky layer'.

claims.text: Per-operator breakdown is reported because the aggregate hides the interesting failure -- one operator scoring zero while the rest score well is a blind spot, and it averages away into a respectable-looking total.
claims.why: The function returns per_operator dict with per-operator n, detected, layers, rate, and also overall rate. The docstring explains why; the code implements that breakdown.

observations.what: render function uses string formatting with fixed-width columns; assumes rep['results'] is a list of dicts with specific keys.
main function has three arms: --held-out, --specificity, and default. All write JSON to runs/eval/ directory.
held_out function imports generate from .mutate and uses attributes last_filtered and last_rejected on generate; these may not exist.
held_out catches SyntaxError, ValueError, RecursionError when comparing before/after; these exceptions are silently ignored (continue).
held_out returns a dict with keys including filtered_sites and rejected_mutations which are populated from generate attributes that may be empty or missing.
